hints.title: Collision Equivalence
hints.text: When two identical entities meet and reverse directions, the collective movement is indistinguishable from passing through each other.

hints.title: Individual Distance to Edges
hints.text: An ant moving left from position p needs p units of time to fall off. An ant moving right from position p needs n - p units of time.

hints.title: Global Maximum Time
hints.text: The last moment corresponds to the maximum distance any individual ant must walk to reach an exit edge.

hints.title: See the blueprint

complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating discrete second-by-second collisions and reversals is complex and unnecessary.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Recognizing collision symmetry reduces the problem to an instantaneous O(1) space max reduction.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Candidate articulates that collisions preserve the set of ant trajectories as if they passed through each other.
complexity.notes: Classic physics brainteaser applied to algorithmic reasoning.
